SEO AND STRUCTURED DATA Use get-seo/list-seo before set-seo or set-schema. Follow the current target schema: record and term SEO are not interchangeable. Yoast-dependent operations require Yoast active. get-seo shows whether Yoast is active; when Yoast is missing, ask the site admin to install and activate it. Preserve SEO properties the user did not ask to change. Inspect inherited/default values before overriding. Custom schema is validated structured data; never treat JSON-LD fields as arbitrary JavaScript insertion. Use real content values and appropriate schema types, not fabricated ratings or claims.
SEO often is not visible in a screenshot. Verify title, meta tags, canonical/robots/social output and structured data in the response/page source; a saved setting does not prove frontend output. Avoid duplicate/conflicting graph entities. Rendering still belongs to the installed SEO plugin and theme.
WHICH TOOL FOR WHICH SCOPE One record or one term: get-seo / set-seo {contentId} / {termId}. Post-type, archive and site-wide SEO settings are read and changed by an administrator in Yoast's settings in wp-admin; no tool reads them.
YOAST VARIABLES IN TITLES AND DESCRIPTIONS An unknown variable is removed from the output without an error, so use only these: %%title%% %%excerpt%% %%excerpt_only%% %%date%% %%modified%% %%id%% %%name%% (author) %%parent_title%% %%focuskw%% %%sitename%% %%sitedesc%% %%sep%% %%page%% %%pagenumber%% %%pagetotal%% %%currentyear%% %%currentdate%% %%category%% %%primary_category%% %%tag%% %%pt_single%% %%pt_plural%% On a term: %%term_title%% %%term_description%% %%category_description%% %%tag_description%% %%term_hierarchy%%. Fields: %%cf_<meta key>%% (a meta value), %%ct_<taxonomy>%% (a record's terms of that taxonomy). %%sitename%% is the WordPress site title (get-site-settings), not the Yoast website name. In set-schema the tokens are different: {{title}} {{url}} {{site_url}} {{excerpt}} {{featured_image}} {{date_published}} {{date_modified}} {{meta:<key>}} {{term:<taxonomy>}}; {{excerpt}} there is Yoast's description for the page.
